# Rule Catalog

<!-- Generated by `dbt-quality rules --format markdown` from rules/*.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every rule, the practice it protects, and the signal that detects it. Load this when a user asks why a rule fired, disputes a suggestion, or you are adding a rule. For one rule's full record — long description, remediation and examples — run `dbt-quality rules --code <CODE>` or call the MCP `rules` tool with `code`.

## Tiers

| Tier | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `universal` | Applies to native and migrated projects when enabled and not waived. |
| `architecture` | Architecture guidance. Migration detection can suppress these findings; the report counts them separately for later review. |
| `migration` | Conversion-related guidance, gated by each detector's migration signals. Migration detection does not suppress these findings. |

Suppression is a review policy, not proof that the code is correct. Disabled rules and waivers
still apply to all tiers. Missing inputs and detector failures produce coverage gaps.

## Disable or waive a rule

Use the narrowest scope that fits. Prefer a waiver for an accepted trade-off or false positive
rather than disabling the rule for the entire run.

| Mechanism | Scope | Effect on the report |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled_rules:` | One rule for the run | Listed as skipped, so readers know it was not checked. |
| `ignore:` config entry | One rule at matching paths | Removed from outputs and counts. |
| `-- dbt-quality: ignore-file <ids>` | One rule in one file | Removed from outputs and counts. |
| `-- dbt-quality: ignore <ids>` | One rule at a reported line | Removed from outputs and counts. |

Use full rule codes. A line directive applies to the line it is on or the line immediately below
it. Place it at the diagnostic's reported location. Config-related rules often anchor at
`{{ config() }}`, but precise read-site rules can report another line. Use `ignore-file` only
when a file-wide waiver is intended. Project- and portfolio-scoped findings need a configuration
waiver; their `file` can be a directory or `<portfolio>`.

If an expected finding is missing, search for `dbt-quality: ignore` and inspect the nearest
`.dbt-quality.yml` for `ignore` and `disabled_rules`. The configuration may be in an ancestor of
the audit root. See the plugin README for configuration lookup and usage examples.

## Codes, kind, level, and severity

Each rule has a code of the form `SSC-{KIND}-DBT{CAT}{NNNN}`. `SSC` is also used by SnowConvert.
Identify this engine's markers by the full shape, including the three-letter pack and four-digit
number. The `DBT` text alone is not enough: SnowConvert also emits codes such as `SSC-EWI-DBT0001`.
Its markers, including `SSC-EWI-SSIS0033`, remain separate from dbt-quality markers.

Three fields classify a finding. They describe the rule's concern, diagnostic level, and impact;
they are not measured probabilities or proof of a defect.

| Kind | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `EWI` | An issue or pattern that needs review. |
| `FDM` | A possible functional difference from source behavior. |
| `PRF` | A performance or cost concern. |

| Level | How to read it |
| --- | --- |
| `error` | The rule treats the detected condition as an error. Confirm its evidence and context before changing code. |
| `warning` | Review a likely problem or risk. |
| `information` | Check a context-dependent pattern; the current code may be appropriate. |

| Severity | Potential impact if the concern applies |
| --- | --- |
| `critical` | Secret exposure, data loss, or a model that produces no rows. |
| `high` | Wrong results. |
| `medium` | Avoidable cost or maintenance work. |
| `low` | Style or a small maintenance concern. |

`level` and `severity` are independent. An `information` finding can have `critical` impact if its
condition applies. Explain that condition instead of treating severity as certainty.

## References and local policy

Each rule's full record includes sources for its guidance. Read those sources with the stated
conditions and version limits. A source can explain a feature without requiring this linter's
threshold or policy. Review thresholds, preferred layouts, and migration conventions are local
choices unless the reference explicitly requires them. Preserve business behavior when applying
advice; a successful dbt build alone does not prove it correct.

## ARC — Architecture & lineage `architecture`

| Rule | Kind | Level | Severity | Tier | Scope | Name | Signal |
| ---- | ---- | ----- | -------- | ---- | ----- | ---- | ------ |
| SSC-EWI-DBTARC0001 | EWI | information | low | architecture | model | Model outside a recognised layer folder | The model path does not match a layer folder recognised by this linter. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTARC0003 | EWI | information | medium | architecture | model | source() used outside the staging layer | A silver or gold model calls source() directly instead of reading a staging model. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTARC0004 | EWI | information | medium | architecture | project | Source table has more than one staging model | Two or more bronze models read the same source table. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTARC0005 | EWI | information | medium | architecture | model | Dependency flows against the layer order | A model depends on a parent in a later layer of the local bronze-to-silver-to-gold order. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTARC0006 | EWI | information | low | architecture | model | Staging model contains joins or aggregation | A bronze staging model contains a join or an aggregation. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTARC0007 | EWI | information | low | architecture | project | Nested folder repeats a parent's tags | A nested folder in dbt_project.yml repeats a tag it already inherits. |

## COL — Column contract vs scai DDL `migration`

| Rule | Kind | Level | Severity | Tier | Scope | Name | Signal |
| ---- | ---- | ----- | -------- | ---- | ----- | ---- | ------ |
| SSC-EWI-DBTCOL0001 | EWI | warning | medium | migration | model | Model matches more than one scai DDL table | More than one table in the scai DDL has the model's relation name, so the column checks cannot pick one. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTCOL0002 | EWI | warning | high | migration | model | DDL column missing from the model | A column of the scai DDL table has no matching output column in the model. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTCOL0003 | EWI | warning | medium | migration | model | Model column not in the DDL | An output column of the model has no column with the same name in the scai DDL table. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTCOL0004 | EWI | information | low | migration | model | Output column cannot be checked against the DDL | An item of the outer SELECT is `*`, Jinja only, or an expression with no alias. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTCOL0005 | EWI | warning | medium | migration | model | Column type differs from the DDL | An output column has no explicit cast, or its cast type differs from the scai DDL type. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTCOL0006 | EWI | warning | medium | migration | model | Column collation differs from the DDL | A text output column has a collation that differs from the COLLATE in the scai DDL. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTCOL0007 | EWI | warning | low | migration | portfolio | scai DDL file not read | A file in `ddl_paths` did not parse, or its columns differ from the scai registry. |

## SQL — Query construction `universal`

| Rule | Kind | Level | Severity | Tier | Scope | Name | Signal |
| ---- | ---- | ----- | -------- | ---- | ----- | ---- | ------ |
| SSC-EWI-DBTSQL0001 | EWI | information | low | universal | project | Derived-table subquery in FROM or JOIN | A SELECT in FROM or JOIN could be a named CTE, or a shared model if other models use the same logic. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTSQL0002 | EWI | information | low | universal | portfolio | Repeated SQL block across models | The same normalized CTE body appears in two or more models in the audit. |

| SSC-EWI-DBTSQL0004 | EWI | information | low | universal | model | Window filter in a nested query | A nested query calculates a window result that an outer WHERE filters without QUALIFY. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTSQL0005 | EWI | information | medium | universal | model | SELECT * outside the staging layer | SELECT * reads directly from a ref() or source() outside the staging layer. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTSQL0006 | EWI | information | high | universal | model | Literal relation read without ref or source | A literal relation or stage read bypasses ref/source lineage; variable-built reads and producer cycles have separate rules. |

| SSC-EWI-DBTSQL0010 | EWI | information | low | universal | model | Unreferenced CTE | A CTE is defined but has no reference outside its own body. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTSQL0011 | EWI | information | low | universal | model | Complex SELECT without named CTEs | A model has joins, aggregates, windows, or set operations but no named CTEs. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTSQL0012 | EWI | information | low | universal | model | UNION removes duplicate rows | UNION without ALL removes duplicates from the combined result. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTSQL0013 | EWI | information | low | universal | model | SELECT DISTINCT may hide a grain problem | SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate projected rows and warrants a check of the intended row grain. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTSQL0014 | EWI | warning | high | universal | model | Conditional ref or source without a dependency hint | A ref() or source() appears under checked Jinja control flow without an unconditional call or dependency hint. |

| SSC-EWI-DBTTST0007 | EWI | information | low | universal | project | Singular test may be reusable as a generic test | A single-table null or count assertion without joins may fit a reusable generic test. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTTST0008 | EWI | information | low | universal | project | Test failure storage is not enabled | No enabling store_failures setting was found under data_tests or tests in dbt_project.yml. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTTST0009 | EWI | warning | high | universal | project | Snapshot configuration is incomplete | A SQL snapshot lacks unique_key or strategy, or the timestamp/check strategy lacks its required field. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTTST0010 | EWI | warning | medium | universal | project | Model and YAML property entry do not match | A model has no detected YAML property entry, or a YAML entry has no detected model. |
| SSC-EWI-DBTTST0012 | EWI | information | medium | universal | model | Key-shaped column has no recognized key test | A model with an existing key test has another key-shaped column without recognized key coverage. |

---

## Naming-policy history

The general naming-convention rules ARC002 (layer prefix) and ARC008 (filename case) were removed.
Their IDs are retired and must not be reused. No column-naming rule was added. MIG0007 still
flags ETL-instance names for review; it does not establish that those names are invalid.

The original decision followed `dbt-modeling`'s Name-Retention Policy: a migrated model can keep
its source object's name. A useful naming check would need a reliable source-to-target mapping.
The migration output reviewed at the time did not provide one inside the project:

- `/* Original Object: ... */` was a comment, not a required structured manifest field.
- Header identifiers varied by platform: 2-part `[owner].[object]` or 3-part
  `[database].[schema].[object]` forms.
- Two header templates existed, and enforcement was warning-only.
- `meta.original_object`, `source_object`, and a crosswalk file were absent from that output.
- The source-to-target mapping was in SnowConvert's external `MIGRATION_REGISTRY`.

These are the recorded reasons for the removal, not universal claims about every dbt project.
The recorded self-audit produced 18 naming findings, most allowed by the retention policy. The
current Rust provenance code still infers platform signals; it does not prove original object
names. Do not restore the naming rule behind a config flag. Reconsider it only with an explicit,
reliable provenance contract.

## Conversion and operational guidance

The generated MIG and OPS tables above are the source of rule IDs, levels, severities, and
signals. Use a rule's full record for its remediation and references; do not maintain a second
copy of those tables here.

MIG0003 and SQL0008 can describe the same finding when an FDM marker concerns ordering and the SQL
uses `ORDER BY (SELECT null)`. Read the marker before grouping them. Do not assume every FDM
marker concerns ordering or that an EWI marker alone proves the SQL cannot compile.

OPS0002 concerns literal credentials in tracked files. PRJ0004 concerns `profiles.yml` placement.
Keep those concerns separate: a profile's presence alone does not prove credential exposure.
Likewise, an installed package or configured hook does not prove that its operational task ran.

## Provenance signals

Automatic migration detection uses the following local weights and a threshold of 4. These are
linter heuristics, not dbt requirements. One weak signal does not suppress all architecture rules.

| Signal | Weight |
| --- | ---: |
| `.scai/config/project.yml` present | 4 |
| `SSC-EWI` / `SSC-FDM` / `!!!RESOLVE EWI!!!` / `NEEDS-USER` markers | 4 |
| `.dbt-quality.yml` `migration.paths` match | 4 |
| `Output/ETL/{Package}/{DataFlow}` layout | 3 |
| `etl_dml_operation__` or `DD_*` constants | 3 |
| `stg_raw__` prefix | 3 |
| Converter placeholders in `dbt_project.yml` | 3 |
| ETL instance names in model names | 2 |

Marker detection uses text with waiver directives blanked by `waivers::blank_directives`. A waiver
contains a rule ID that can resemble a conversion marker. Without blanking, waivers could falsely
classify a native project as a migration. Owned dbt-quality markers are also blanked during discovery.

A score of at least 7 gives `high` confidence and permits project-wide architecture suppression.
A score of 4-6 gives `medium` confidence and covers files with detected migration signals; findings
with no file location can also be suppressed. Explicit `migration.mode: lift_and_shift` covers the
project; `native` skips automatic provenance classification. Inspect the recorded reasons before
accepting the scope, especially in a project with both migrated and native code.

The retired dbt-validation package's `check_migration_header` rule was not carried over. It used
broad source-platform substrings and a block-comment match for `Source`, rather than a structured
provenance check. Its acceptance did not prove a reliable original-object mapping. This history
explains why a replacement needs a declared contract rather than another naming heuristic.

## Adding a rule

### Diagnostic wording

State what the detector observed, the possible consequence, and the condition under which a change
is needed. Use direct wording for a verified condition. Do not turn a local policy into an upstream
requirement or treat a diagnostic level as proof that every matching model is wrong.

An information-level finding must explain when the code is acceptable. For example:
"Verify `unique_key` is set; correct as-is if the load is append-only and duplicates are acceptable."

An error-level rule still needs evidence-specific wording. A literal relation reference can bypass
dbt dependency tracking without being invalid SQL. A conversion marker can require review without
proving that the model cannot run. PRJ0004 reports profile placement at `warning` when untracked or
Git status is unknown, and at `information` when Git-ignored. Credential content belongs to OPS0002.

Use humanizer and ASD-STE100 principles: short sentences, clear subjects, active voice, and consistent
terms. Do not claim certified compliance. Keep exact code identifiers and executable examples.

### Implementation steps

1. Add a record to `rules/<PACK>.json`, sorted by `number`, with every required field from
   `rules/schema.json`: name, descriptions, remediation, level, severity, tier, scope, effort,
   `since`, and at least one example. The record is the source of rule metadata. `cargo build`
   rejects invalid metadata, duplicate codes, and pack/code mismatches.
2. Add official references that support the actual guidance. Keep the long description's References
   list consistent with the structured `references` array. State version limits and local policy
   choices. Keep names single-line and at most 60 characters, without annotation/Jinja delimiters;
   keep short descriptions at most 160 characters.
3. Add the detector in `ai/crates/dbt-quality/dbt-quality-core/src/rules/<pack>.rs` and register it in
   `DETECTORS` with `Detect::Model`, `Detect::Project`, or `Detect::Portfolio`. Its scope must match
   the record. A test checks that records and detectors correspond.
4. Build findings with `Suggestion::new(code, message)`, evidence, and finding-specific remediation
   where needed. Use `.span(...)` for a real match offset. Otherwise the anchor layer uses the
   `{{ config() }}` block for config rules, a schema YAML model entry for test/doc rules, or the
   first query token, with line 1 as a fallback. Report a column only when a real offset is known.
5. Add a positive test and a clean counterpart with `crate::testing::TempProject`. Include valid
   exceptions and missing-input cases. Confirm both that the intended pattern fires and that the
   accepted form stays silent.
6. Regenerate the catalog with `scripts/build-catalog.sh`, which writes `docs/rule-catalog.md`.
   `scripts/check-catalog.sh` fails when the committed copy differs. Run the Rust tests and report
   checks before treating the change as complete.
